foodName: Cucumber and yogurt salad (Kheere aur dahi ka salad)
dishTitle: Cucumber and Yogurt Salad (Kheere aur Dahi ka Salad)
instructions: Wash the cucumber thoroughly.
Peel it if required and cut it into small pieces.
Take plain yogurt in a mixing bowl and whisk until smooth.
Add cucumber pieces to the yogurt.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and lemon juice.
Mix all ingredients properly.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve fresh.
Place eggs in boiling water for 9-10 minutes. Cool in iced water, peel, and slice into halves.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add chopped onion and slit green chilli; sauté over medium heat for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, and salt; cook for 3 minutes until tomato breaks down.
Pour 1.5 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil.
Stir in the rolled oats, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 4 minutes until thick and creamy.
Transfer savory oats to a bowl, top with sliced boiled eggs, and serve warm.
Spoon chilled Greek yogurt into a clean breakfast bowl.
Rinse fresh berries under cold water and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Slice larger strawberries into quarters.
Arrange berries over the yogurt surface.
Scatter chia seeds and dust with a gentle pinch of cinnamon.
Serve immediately or chill for 10 minutes before enjoying.
Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve to remove natural saponin.
Add quinoa to a pot with 1 cup of water and a pinch of salt; simmer covered for 12-14 minutes until water is absorbed.
Heat 1 teaspoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add paneer cubes and sear for 2-3 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Wash baby spinach, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes.
In a wide meal bowl, layer the warm fluffy quinoa.
Arrange seared paneer, fresh spinach leaves, cucumber, and tomatoes side by side.
Drizzle fresh lemon juice and season with cracked black pepper and salt.

dishTitle: Spiced Roasted Makhana with Fragrant Chai
instructions: Heat ghee in a wide heavy kadai over low flame.
Add makhana and dry-roast continuously for 6-8 minutes until crisp and brittle to the touch.
Dust roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and black salt over the warm makhana; toss well to coat.
In a saucepan, bring water, crushed cardamom, and tea leaves to a boil for 2 minutes.
Add milk and simmer for 2 minutes until rich and aromatic.
Strain tea into a cup and serve warm alongside the crunchy spiced makhana.

dishTitle: Homestyle Dal, Phulka Roti & Seasonal Greens

ingredients.name: Yellow moong dal or toor dal

instructions: Rinse dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and half teaspoon salt for 3 whistles.
Knead whole wheat flour with water into a supple dough, divide into 2 balls, roll thin, and roast on a hot tawa until puffed.
Wash and finely chop the seasonal greens.
Heat ½ teaspoon oil in a pan, add minced garlic, and sauté chopped greens with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes.
In a small tadka pan, heat ½ teaspoon ghee, splutter cumin seeds, and fry chopped onion and tomato until soft.
Pour tadka into the cooked dal, mix well, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve warm tempered dal with fresh hot phulkas and garlic-sautéed greens.
In a small bowl, mix grated cheese, minced green chillies, diced capsicum, and black pepper.
Spread the cheesy chilli mixture evenly over one slice of bread.
Cover with the second slice and lightly press down.
Smear half teaspoon butter on the outside bread surface.
Toast on a medium-hot tawa or sandwich toaster for 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and golden and cheese melts.
Cut diagonally and serve hot.
Trim bread crusts if desired, or keep intact for added fiber.
Spread fresh mint-coriander chutney evenly on one side of each bread slice.
Wash, peel, and thinly slice the fresh cucumber.
Layer cucumber rounds closely over the bottom bread slice.
Sprinkle roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and a dash of black salt.
Close with the top bread slice, press gently, and slice diagonally into triangles.
Serve fresh and crisp.

foodName: Cheese and pineapple sandwich (Cheese aur ananas ka sandwich)
instructions: Pat the pineapple pieces completely dry using a kitchen towel to prevent soggy bread.
Combine grated cheese, chopped pineapple, and cracked black pepper in a small bowl.
Distribute the mixture evenly across one bread slice.
Top with the other slice and lightly butter the outer sides.
Toast on a medium pan or grill press for 2 minutes per side until golden brown and cheese is melted.
Slice in half and serve warm.

foodName: Cheese and tomato sandwich (Cheese aur tamatar ke sandwich)
instructions: Spread green chutney or herb spread evenly over both bread slices.
Place cheese over the base slice.
Arrange thin tomato slices neatly over the cheese.
Season lightly with black pepper, oregano, and salt.
Cover with the second slice, press gently, and slice into halves.
Enjoy fresh.

foodName: Peanut and tomato sandwich (Moongfali aur tamatar ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Peanut and Tomato Sandwich (Moongfali aur Tamatar ka Sandwich)

ingredients.name: Freshly ground black pepper & sea salt

instructions: Lightly toast bread slices if desired for a crisp texture.
Spread unsweetened peanut butter evenly across one bread slice.
Arrange fresh ripe tomato slices on top of the peanut butter layer.
Sprinkle cracked black pepper, a touch of sea salt, and fresh herbs.
Cap with the remaining bread slice and slice neatly in half.
Serve immediately.

foodName: Carrot apple sandwich (Gajar aur seb ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Carrot Apple Sandwich (Gajar aur Seb ka Sandwich)
instructions: Grate carrot and apple into a glass bowl.
Toss immediately with lemon juice to keep apple fresh and prevent browning.
Add shredded mint leaves, cracked black pepper, and black salt; mix well.
Pile the crunchy carrot-apple slaw generously onto a bread slice.
Cover with the second slice, press softly, and cut in half.
Serve as a revitalizing vegan lunch or snack.

foodName: Pea potato sandwich (toasted) (Matar aloo ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Toasted Pea and Potato Sandwich (Matar Aloo ka Sandwich)
instructions: In a bowl, mix mashed boiled potato, crushed green peas, spices, salt, and fresh coriander.
Spread the spiced vegetable filling evenly between two bread slices.
Brush a few drops of oil on the outside of the bread.
Toast on a hot skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden and crunchy.
Slice into triangles and serve with homemade mint chutney.

foodName: Pea keema sandwich (toasted) (Matar aur keema ka sandwich)

ingredients.name: Coarsely minced green peas & soya granules

instructions: Heat oil in a pan, sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste until aromatic.
Add crushed peas and soaked minced soya keema with spices and salt.
Cook for 4-5 minutes until dry and well combined, then cool slightly.
Place savory plant keema between bread slices.
Grill or pan-toast with minimal oil until deeply crisp.
Serve warm.
Mix mashed potato or crumbled silken tofu with salt and chili flakes.
Spread a thin layer over one side of the bread slices to act as a binder.
Press sesame seeds firmly into the layer so the surface is thoroughly covered.
Heat oil in a flat pan and place toast seed-side down over medium flame.
Cook for 3 minutes until sesame seeds turn fragrant and golden, flip and toast reverse side for 2 minutes.
Serve hot and crunchy.
Dry roast cracked wheat in a pressure cooker or saucepan for 3-4 minutes until nutty and light brown.
Pour in water, close the lid, and pressure cook on medium flame for 3 whistles (or simmer 15 mins in pot).
Release steam naturally and open the cooker.
Stir in jaggery powder and fragrant cardamom powder over low flame until melted.
Garnish with slivered almonds and serve warm.
In a dry saucepan, gently roast suji on low heat for 3 minutes until aromatic.
Slowly pour water or oat milk while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook over low flame for 4-5 minutes until smooth and gently thickened.
Fold in jaggery and cardamom powder, stirring until uniformly sweet.
Top with crushed walnuts and enjoy hot.
Combine rolled oats and water or soy milk in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then turn down heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring frequently until creamy.
Remove from heat, pour into a breakfast bowl, and arrange fresh banana slices on top.
Sprinkle cinnamon and ground flaxseed for omega-3 richness.

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds & turmeric
ingredients.quantity: ½ tsp mustard, ¼ tsp turmeric

instructions: Rinse rice flakes in a colander under running water for 30 seconds; drain completely and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves, green chilli, and diced onion.
Sauté until onion turns soft and translucent, then add turmeric powder and salt.
Stir in the softened poha and roasted peanuts gently so flakes do not break.
Cover with a lid and let steam on lowest heat for 2 minutes.
Finish with fresh lemon juice and chopped coriander leaves.
Heat half teaspoon oil in a large kadai over low flame.
Add curry leaves, roasted gram, and turmeric powder, letting them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add puffed rice and toss continuously for 3-4 minutes until extra crisp.
Season with rock salt and chaat masala.
Cool slightly and serve as a light, crunchy tea-time snack.
In a mixing bowl, combine besan, ajwain, turmeric, and salt.
Gradually whisk in water to make a smooth, pourable batter without lumps.
Fold in grated carrot, chopped spinach, and finely chopped onion.
Heat a non-stick tawa, brush lightly with oil, and pour a ladleful of batter, spreading into a round.
Cook on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until bubbles appear and underside is golden.
Flip and cook the other side for 2 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with mint or tomato dip.
Add fresh chilled curd, cold water, and raw sugar into a blender or traditional madhani pot.
Blend or churn vigorously for 45-60 seconds until a thick, velvety foam forms on top.
Add cardamom powder and rose water; give one final quick pulse.
Pour into a tall clay kulhad or glass, ensuring the rich froth sits on top.
Serve refreshingly cold.
Combine chilled curd, water, roasted cumin powder, and black salt in a blender.
Whisk or blend for 1 minute until smooth and frothy.
Pour into a chilled glass.
Garnish with crushed fresh mint leaves and a pinch of roasted cumin.
Serve as an invigorating digestive cooler.
Gently place eggs into a small saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch.
Bring water to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.
Once boiling, turn off heat, cover tightly with a lid, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Transfer eggs immediately to a bowl filled with iced water for 3 minutes to stop cooking.
Gently tap and peel shells under running water.
Slice eggs into halves, season with black pepper and rock salt, and serve.
Mash or slice the boiled egg in a bowl and mix with chopped onion, black pepper, and chaat masala.
Spread green chutney on both bread slices.
Layer the seasoned egg mixture generously over the bottom slice.
Top with second bread slice and lightly toast on a griddle with ½ teaspoon butter until golden crisp.
Cut in half and serve warm.

ingredients.name: Hung curd or light yogurt spread

instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted simmering water for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
Shred the chicken using two forks and let it cool slightly.
In a bowl, mix shredded chicken with hung curd, black pepper, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt.
Place crisp lettuce leaf and sliced cucumber on one bread slice.
Spoon creamy chicken spread evenly over the greens.
Cover with second slice, slice diagonally, and enjoy.
Spread mint-coriander green chutney on inner sides of both bread slices.
Layer warm cooked chicken shreds and crunchy sliced peppers on bread.
Close sandwich and press gently.
Brush skillet with olive oil, place sandwich, and toast over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve warm with fresh tomato dip.
In a salad bowl, blend light mayonnaise with grated carrot, cucumber, and sweet corn.
Season with freshly ground black pepper and a touch of salt.
Spread the chilled vegetable mayonnaise mixture thickly between two slices of whole wheat bread.
Trim edges if preferred and cut diagonally into finger sandwiches.
Serve fresh and crisp.

foodName: Egg and tomato sandwich (Ande aur tamatar ka sandwich)
dishTitle: Egg and Tomato Sandwich (Ande aur Tamatar ka Sandwich)
instructions: Lightly toast multigrain bread slices.
Spread mustard or chutney across both slices.
Alternate layers of sliced boiled egg and juicy red tomato rounds.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper and sea salt.
Top with the second slice, slice across, and serve immediately.

dishTitle: Indian Style Scrambled Eggs (Ande ki Bhurji)
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat lightly with a fork.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat; sauté chopped onion and green chilli until golden.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, and chili powder; sauté for 2 minutes until softened.
Lower the flame and pour in the beaten eggs.
Stir gently and continuously for 2-3 minutes as soft curds form; do not overcook.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves and serve warm with roti or toast.
Fill a deep pan with water, add vinegar, and bring to a gentle, steady simmer (not a rolling boil).
Crack one cold egg into a small ramekin or teacup.
Swirl the simmering water with a spoon to create a gentle whirlpool in the center.
Carefully drop the egg into the whirlpool eye; the swirling water wraps whites around the yolk.
Poach gently for 3-4 minutes until whites are firm and yolk remains softly liquid.
Lift with a slotted spoon, blot on paper towel, season with pepper and salt, and serve on toast.
Warm oil or butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Carefully crack eggs directly into the pan without breaking the yolks.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set and edges turn slightly golden.
Spoon a little warm oil over whites if needed to finish setting.
Slide onto a plate, dust with sea salt and cracked black pepper, and serve warm.
In a small skillet, sauté sliced mushrooms, onion, and spinach with a pinch of salt for 2 minutes; set aside.
Whisk eggs in a bowl with salt, black pepper, and oregano until slightly bubbly.
Heat oil in an 8-inch non-stick skillet over medium-low flame.
Pour beaten eggs into skillet and tilt pan so it spreads into an even round.
When eggs are almost set on top, spoon the warm mushroom-spinach filling onto one half.
Gently fold the other half over the filling into a neat semicircle.
Cook for 30 seconds more and slide onto a warm plate.
Season chicken cubes with olive oil, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Sear on a hot grill pan or skillet for 4-5 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Wash salad greens, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes in ice-cold water, then spin dry.
Assemble chilled greens in a large bowl and top with warm grilled chicken.
Drizzle lemon juice and freshly cracked black pepper.
Toss lightly and serve fresh.
In a soup pot, bring chicken broth, minced ginger, and sweet corn to a boil.
Add minced chicken and simmer for 5-6 minutes until chicken is tender.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and slowly pour into the simmering soup, stirring until thickened.
Turn down flame and slowly drizzle the beaten egg white in a thin stream while gently stirring to create delicate silky ribbons.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle chopped spring onion greens, and serve hot.
Warm milk in a small saucepan over low heat until steam gently rises (do not boil).
In a bowl, whisk egg yolk with jaggery and vanilla until pale and creamy.
Gradually pour 3 tablespoons of warm milk into the yolk while whisking briskly to temper.
Pour tempered yolk mixture back into the saucepan with remaining milk.
Cook over lowest heat for 3-4 minutes while stirring constantly until mixture lightly coats a spoon.
Pour into a mug, dust freshly grated nutmeg and cinnamon on top, and enjoy warm or chilled.
Grate fresh cucumber and gently squeeze out excess water with your palms.
Whisk plain yogurt in a mixing bowl until silky smooth.
Fold the grated cucumber into the whipped yogurt.
Add roasted cumin powder, black salt, and finely chopped mint leaves.
Mix thoroughly, chill in refrigerator for 10 minutes, and serve cold.

foodName: Tomato onion raita (Tamatar aur pyaaz ka raita)
dishTitle: Tomato Onion Raita (Tamatar aur Pyaaz ka Raita)
instructions: Whisk yogurt until creamy and lump-free.
Add finely diced onion, tomato, and minced green chilli.
Stir in roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve chilled alongside rice, pulao, or roti.
Optionally steam sprouted moong for 2 minutes or use fresh raw sprouts for maximum crunch.
In a wide mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong, diced cucumber, and tomato.
Add bright pomegranate arils and chopped fresh coriander.
Drizzle freshly squeezed lemon juice over the mixture.
Season with chaat masala and black salt, toss lightly, and serve.
In a large bowl, place cooked, drained, room-temperature pulses.
Add diced bell peppers, crunchy carrots, and fresh cucumber.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, roasted cumin, black pepper, and salt in a cup.
Pour dressing over pulses and vegetables; toss gently until evenly coated.
Serve as a protein-dense vegan meal or side.
Immerse green leaves in ice-cold water for 5 minutes, then dry thoroughly in a spinner.
Tear greens into bite-sized pieces and arrange in a wide salad bowl.
Scatter sliced cucumber, radish rounds, and julienned carrots.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil and fresh lemon juice over the top.
Season with freshly cracked black pepper and rock salt, toss lightly, and serve at once.
Rinse dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles.
Heat ghee or oil in a pan, crackle cumin and mustard seeds.
Add chopped onion and ginger-garlic paste, sautéing until fragrant and light golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and ground spices; cook until oil separates and tomatoes turn mushy.
Pour cooked dal into the tempering pan, add a little water if too thick, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and serve warm.
Wash moong dal until water runs clear.
Simmer dal in a pot with water, turmeric, grated ginger, and salt for 15 minutes until soft.
In a small pan, heat 1 teaspoon oil and splutter cumin seeds.
Add chopped tomato and cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour the fragrant tomato cumin tadka directly into the simmering moong dal.
Simmer together for 2 minutes, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve.
Blanch washed spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water to retain vibrant green color.
Blend blanched spinach with green chilli into a smooth puree.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds, minced garlic, ginger, and onion; sauté until translucent.
Add tomato puree, salt, and spices; cook until oil releases.
Pour in bright green spinach puree and simmer gently for 3-4 minutes.
Gently fold in fresh paneer cubes and warm through for 2 minutes.
Serve warm with phulkas or brown rice.
Rinse rice and moong dal together until water runs clear; soak for 15 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, splutter cumin seeds and black peppercorns.
Add grated ginger and turmeric powder, sautéing for 20 seconds.
Add drained rice and dal, stirring for 1 minute to coat with ghee and spices.
Pour in 3 cups of water and salt; close cooker lid.
Cook for 4 whistles on medium heat, then allow steam to subside naturally.
Open and stir lightly into a creamy comforting consistency; serve warm with curd.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot, add whole spices until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown.
Toss in mixed diced vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add drained basmati rice and gently stir for 1 minute without breaking grains.
Pour 1 cup hot water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Cover tightly, turn heat to lowest setting, and cook undisturbed for 12 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes off heat, fluff gently with a fork, and serve.

ingredients.name: Turmeric, coriander, cumin & red chili powder
Garam masala & fresh coriander
ingredients.quantity: ¼ tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp coriander

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot, add whole cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté over medium heat until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until raw aroma dissipates.
Add pureed tomato and ground spices; cook until oil begins to separate from the masala.
Add chicken pieces and sear in the masala for 4-5 minutes until sealed.
Pour in ½ cup warm water, cover with lid, and simmer over low heat for 12-14 minutes until chicken is tender and juicy.
Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander, stir, and serve with rotis or steamed rice.
